newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP says can lower Magma costs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP says can lower Magma costs.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd chief executive officer John Prescott said on Wednesday that BHP could lower costs of production at its U.S. Magma Copper unit from its current levels of around 85 U.S. cents per pound.
"There is no doubt that we can improve on the 85 (U.S.) cents," Prescott told reporters after giving an address to the Australia-Israel Chamber of Commerce.
Prescott said Magma Copper's costs of production had been around 68 U.S. cents per pound at the time that BHP bought Magma for US$2.4 billion, which was finalised in January this year.
"I don't expect copper prices to rebound...for some time to come, so then we're critically dependent on our own efforts at getting the costs down," Prescott said.
BHP's other major copper mines Escondida in Chile and Ok Tedi in Papua New Guinea produce copper at about 40 U.S. cents per pound. Magma Copper unit made a loss in the quarter ended August 31, 1996.
Net profit before minorities from BHP's copper division was A$85 million for the August quarter, 55 percent lower on the same quarter a year earlier because of lower prices.
On Tuesday, December COMEX copper settled 1.50 U.S. cents firmer at 89.15 cents per pound.
At 2.35 p.m (0435 GMT), BHP shares were 14 cents up at A$16.06, off its high of A$16.20 hit earlier on Wednesday.
